spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od15m8p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Instances, Slots, Orders

\* coarseLock models the pool-level lock a matching-desk instance must hold
\* before touching any individual slot; fineLock/claimant model the second,
\* per-slot level of the hierarchy that is actually taken and released while
\* binding one order to one slot.
VARIABLES coarseLock, fineLock, claimant, assigned, pending

vars == <<coarseLock, fineLock, claimant, assigned, pending>>

Init ==
  /\ coarseLock = "none"
  /\ fineLock = [s \in Slots |-> "none"]
  /\ claimant = [s \in Slots |-> "none"]
  /\ assigned = {}
  /\ pending = Orders

AcquireCoarse(inst) ==
  /\ coarseLock = "none"
  /\ coarseLock' = inst
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, claimant, assigned, pending>>

\* A slot can only be fine-locked if no order already owns it: this guard is
\* what actually prevents the shared pool from double-allocating a slot.
AcquireFine(inst, s) ==
  /\ coarseLock = inst
  /\ fineLock[s] = "none"
  /\ claimant[s] = "none"
  /\ ~ (\E o2 \in Orders : <<o2, s>> \in assigned)
  /\ \E o \in pending :
       /\ ~ (\E s2 \in Slots : claimant[s2] = o)
       /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![s] = inst]
       /\ claimant' = [claimant EXCEPT ![s] = o]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, assigned, pending>>

CommitAllocation(inst, s) ==
  /\ fineLock[s] = inst
  /\ claimant[s] # "none"
  /\ assigned' = assigned \cup {<<claimant[s], s>>}
  /\ pending' = pending \ {claimant[s]}
  /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![s] = "none"]
  /\ claimant' = [claimant EXCEPT ![s] = "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED coarseLock

ReleaseCoarse(inst) ==
  /\ coarseLock = inst
  /\ coarseLock' = "none"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, claimant, assigned, pending>>

NextInst(inst) ==
  \/ AcquireCoarse(inst)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : AcquireFine(inst, s)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : CommitAllocation(inst, s)
  \/ ReleaseCoarse(inst)

Next == \E inst \in Instances : NextInst(inst)

\* Strong fairness per instance, per hierarchy level: an instance that is
\* never dropped (no crash model here) cannot dodge its own fine-grained
\* work forever by cycling the coarse lock, so it always finishes the
\* acquire-coarse / acquire-fine / commit / release cycle it started.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\
  (\A inst \in Instances :
     /\ SF_vars(AcquireCoarse(inst))
     /\ SF_vars(\E s \in Slots : AcquireFine(inst, s))
     /\ SF_vars(\E s \in Slots : CommitAllocation(inst, s))
     /\ SF_vars(ReleaseCoarse(inst)))

\* Safety: the shared pool never records the same slot against two orders.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
  \A p1, p2 \in assigned : p1[2] = p2[2] => p1[1] = p2[1]

\* Liveness: a pending order is not stuck forever waiting on the shared pool.
SlotsEventuallyAssigned ==
  \A o \in Orders : (o \in pending) ~> (\E s \in Slots : <<o, s>> \in assigned)

====
nl:
Two independent opening-auction engines, run by separate matching-desk instances,
share a single pool of numbered auction slots at market open. A slot is the unit
of work handed to whichever engine processes it: each pending order must be
bound to exactly one slot before the auction can batch and cross it. To bind a
slot, an engine first takes the pool's coarse lock (so only one engine drives
the allocation protocol at a time), then takes that specific slot's fine lock,
then commits the slot to one of the still-pending orders and releases both
locks so the other engine can proceed. Because the two engines pull from the
one shared pool with no static partitioning between them, the coarse-then-fine
locking discipline is the only thing stopping both engines from independently
handing the same slot number to two different orders during the opening cross.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No two distinct orders are ever recorded as holding the same
auction slot at the same time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every order that is still pending eventually gets bound to
some auction slot.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od7m9p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Towers, Blocks, TotalContainers, MaxEpoch

\* epoch/instEpoch/gate model the epoch-numbered reconfiguration: a tower may
\* only cross the yard boundary (unload/load) while it holds the single gate
\* and its own synced epoch matches the yard's current epoch. Reconfiguring
\* the yard bumps the epoch and revokes the gate until a tower re-syncs.
VARIABLES count, reserve, epoch, instEpoch, gate

vars == <<count, reserve, epoch, instEpoch, gate>>

RECURSIVE SumOver(_)
SumOver(S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET b == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
       IN count[b] + SumOver(S \ {b})

Init ==
  /\ count = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
  /\ reserve = TotalContainers
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ instEpoch = [t \in Towers |-> 0]
  /\ gate = "none"

Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ gate' = "none"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<count, reserve, instEpoch>>

SyncTower(t) ==
  /\ instEpoch[t] < epoch
  /\ instEpoch' = [instEpoch EXCEPT ![t] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<count, reserve, epoch, gate>>

AcquireGate(t) ==
  /\ instEpoch[t] = epoch
  /\ gate = "none"
  /\ gate' = t
  /\ UNCHANGED <<count, reserve, epoch, instEpoch>>

Unload(t, b) ==
  /\ gate = t
  /\ instEpoch[t] = epoch
  /\ reserve > 0
  /\ reserve' = reserve - 1
  /\ count' = [count EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, instEpoch, gate>>

Load(t, b) ==
  /\ gate = t
  /\ instEpoch[t] = epoch
  /\ count[b] > 0
  /\ count' = [count EXCEPT ![b] = @ - 1]
  /\ reserve' = reserve + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, instEpoch, gate>>

MoveBlock(t, b1, b2) ==
  /\ gate = t
  /\ instEpoch[t] = epoch
  /\ b1 # b2
  /\ count[b1] > 0
  /\ count' = [count EXCEPT ![b1] = @ - 1, ![b2] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reserve, epoch, instEpoch, gate>>

Next ==
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ \E t \in Towers : SyncTower(t)
  \/ \E t \in Towers : AcquireGate(t)
  \/ \E t \in Towers, b \in Blocks : Unload(t, b)
  \/ \E t \in Towers, b \in Blocks : Load(t, b)
  \/ \E t \in Towers, b1 \in Blocks, b2 \in Blocks : MoveBlock(t, b1, b2)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Conservation: nothing created or destroyed -- reserve plus all block
\* counts must always add up to the fixed fleet size.
Conservation == reserve + SumOver(Blocks) = TotalContainers

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Towers = {t1, t2}
  Blocks = {b1, b2}
  TotalContainers = 4
  MaxEpoch = 2
INVARIANT Conservation
nl:
A container-ship crane yard tracks a fixed fleet of shipping containers that
are either sitting in one of the yard's storage blocks or still held in an
external reserve (on a berthed ship, waiting to be unloaded, or already
loaded out and gone). Two independent crane-control towers, Tower A and Tower
B, share the same yard inventory pool with no static split between them: both
may move containers between blocks, unload a container out of reserve into a
block, or load a container out of a block back into reserve. The yard layout
is periodically reconfigured (new block map, new crane assignments), and each
reconfiguration bumps a global epoch number. A control tower may only unload
or load containers across the yard boundary while it holds the yard's single
boundary gate and its own last-synced epoch matches the yard's current epoch;
a reconfiguration revokes the gate so a tower must re-sync to the new epoch
before it can touch the boundary again. Moves between blocks inside the yard
do not require the boundary gate. Because the two towers draw from the one
shared pool, the epoch fencing on the boundary gate is what stops a
reconfiguration from letting either tower silently create or lose containers
while the yard is being resynchronized.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the number of containers sitting
in reserve plus the total number of containers across all yard blocks equals
the fixed total container count -- no container is ever created or destroyed
by a move, an unload, a load, or a reconfiguration.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od8m1p0t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS N

\* Workers are numbered 1..N around the ring; 0 is reserved for the admin
\* so the occupancy set below stays a plain set of numbers (no mixed types).
Procs == 1..N
AdminId == 0

\* token/PassToken model the ring: the critical section is only reachable by
\* the worker currently holding the token. adminWaiting/ringSuspended model
\* the privileged override: the admin can seize the section directly and,
\* while it does, the ring stops circulating until the admin releases.
VARIABLES token, inCS, reqSet, adminWaiting, ringSuspended

vars == <<token, inCS, reqSet, adminWaiting, ringSuspended>>

Init ==
  /\ token = 1
  /\ inCS = {}
  /\ reqSet = {}
  /\ adminWaiting = FALSE
  /\ ringSuspended = FALSE

Request(p) ==
  /\ p \notin reqSet
  /\ reqSet' = reqSet \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, inCS, adminWaiting, ringSuspended>>

\* Entry requires holding the token, an outstanding request, an empty
\* section, and no live admin override -- this is the guard that actually
\* keeps ring workers and the admin from ever overlapping.
EnterCS(p) ==
  /\ token = p
  /\ p \in reqSet
  /\ inCS = {}
  /\ ~ringSuspended
  /\ inCS' = inCS \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, reqSet, adminWaiting, ringSuspended>>

ExitCS(p) ==
  /\ p \in inCS
  /\ inCS' = inCS \ {p}
  /\ reqSet' = reqSet \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, adminWaiting, ringSuspended>>

PassToken ==
  /\ inCS = {}
  /\ ~ringSuspended
  /\ token' = (token % N) + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inCS, reqSet, adminWaiting, ringSuspended>>

AdminRequest ==
  /\ ~adminWaiting
  /\ adminWaiting' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, inCS, reqSet, ringSuspended>>

AdminSeize ==
  /\ adminWaiting
  /\ inCS = {}
  /\ inCS' = {AdminId}
  /\ ringSuspended' = TRUE
  /\ adminWaiting' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, reqSet>>

AdminRelease ==
  /\ AdminId \in inCS
  /\ inCS' = inCS \ {AdminId}
  /\ ringSuspended' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, reqSet, adminWaiting>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Procs : Request(p)
  \/ \E p \in Procs : EnterCS(p)
  \/ \E p \in Procs : ExitCS(p)
  \/ PassToken
  \/ AdminRequest
  \/ AdminSeize
  \/ AdminRelease

\* The token must keep circulating and a worker's own entry must not be
\* dodged forever by repeated admin interruptions (strong fairness); once
\* a worker or the admin is in, it must eventually leave (weak fairness).
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(PassToken)
  /\ (\A p \in Procs : SF_vars(EnterCS(p)) /\ WF_vars(ExitCS(p)))
  /\ WF_vars(AdminRelease)

\* Safety: never more than one occupant (a ring worker or the admin).
MutualExclusion == Cardinality(inCS) <= 1

\* Liveness: a worker that asks for the section eventually gets in.
RequestsEventuallyServed == \A p \in Procs : (p \in reqSet) ~> (p \in inCS)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  N = 3
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
PROPERTY RequestsEventuallyServed
nl:
A university course-registration system has a fixed set of registration
worker processes arranged in a token ring. Only the worker currently holding
the ring token, and only if it has an outstanding request, may enter the
critical section that edits the shared seat-count record for a popular
capacity-limited section, so that two workers can never interleave writes and
overbook it. A worker that wants to edit the record raises a request flag;
when the token reaches it and it has a raised flag, it may enter the critical
section, and it must eventually leave, dropping its flag. When no one holds
the critical section and the ring is not suspended, the token keeps
circulating to the next worker. On top of the ring, a privileged registrar
admin process can raise its own override request at any time and, once the
critical section is free, seize it directly without waiting for the token --
this suspends the ring until the admin finishes and releases, after which
token circulation resumes. Even during an admin override, the critical
section must never be shared: the admin's occupancy still excludes every
ring worker, and vice versa.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one of the ring workers or the admin is ever inside
the critical section of the seat-count record at the same time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every ring worker that raises a request eventually gets to
enter the critical section, even though the admin can repeatedly interrupt
the ring.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od16m2p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Participants, Prescriptions

\* status/yesVotes/anyNo model the two-phase-commit round per prescription;
\* dispenseCount records how many times the irreversible dispense step has
\* actually fired, so DispenseAtMostOnce is a real check on the protocol
\* rather than something guaranteed by the type of a boolean flag.
VARIABLES status, yesVotes, anyNo, dispenseCount, overrideUsed

vars == <<status, yesVotes, anyNo, dispenseCount, overrideUsed>>

Init ==
  /\ status = [rx \in Prescriptions |-> "pending"]
  /\ yesVotes = [rx \in Prescriptions |-> {}]
  /\ anyNo = [rx \in Prescriptions |-> FALSE]
  /\ dispenseCount = [rx \in Prescriptions |-> 0]
  /\ overrideUsed = [rx \in Prescriptions |-> FALSE]

VoteYes(rx, part) ==
  /\ status[rx] = "pending"
  /\ ~anyNo[rx]
  /\ part \notin yesVotes[rx]
  /\ yesVotes' = [yesVotes EXCEPT ![rx] = @ \cup {part}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<status, anyNo, dispenseCount, overrideUsed>>

VoteNo(rx, part) ==
  /\ status[rx] = "pending"
  /\ part \notin yesVotes[rx]
  /\ anyNo' = [anyNo EXCEPT ![rx] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<status, yesVotes, dispenseCount, overrideUsed>>

\* Normal commit: only once every participant agreed and no one refused.
Commit(rx) ==
  /\ status[rx] = "pending"
  /\ ~anyNo[rx]
  /\ yesVotes[rx] = Participants
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![rx] = "committed"]
  /\ dispenseCount' = [dispenseCount EXCEPT ![rx] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yesVotes, anyNo, overrideUsed>>

Abort(rx) ==
  /\ status[rx] = "pending"
  /\ anyNo[rx]
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![rx] = "aborted"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yesVotes, anyNo, dispenseCount, overrideUsed>>

\* Admin override: forces the irreversible dispense despite a no vote, but
\* only while the prescription is still pending, exactly like the normal
\* commit path -- once settled, neither path can touch it again.
AdminOverrideCommit(rx) ==
  /\ status[rx] = "pending"
  /\ anyNo[rx]
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![rx] = "committed"]
  /\ dispenseCount' = [dispenseCount EXCEPT ![rx] = @ + 1]
  /\ overrideUsed' = [overrideUsed EXCEPT ![rx] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yesVotes, anyNo>>

Next ==
  \/ \E rx \in Prescriptions, part \in Participants : VoteYes(rx, part)
  \/ \E rx \in Prescriptions, part \in Participants : VoteNo(rx, part)
  \/ \E rx \in Prescriptions : Commit(rx)
  \/ \E rx \in Prescriptions : Abort(rx)
  \/ \E rx \in Prescriptions : AdminOverrideCommit(rx)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: dispensing happens at most once per prescription, and it has
\* happened precisely when the prescription is recorded as committed --
\* whichever of the two commit paths (normal or override) got there first.
DispenseAtMostOnce ==
  \A rx \in Prescriptions :
    /\ dispenseCount[rx] \in {0, 1}
    /\ (dispenseCount[rx] = 1 <=> status[rx] = "committed")

====
nl:
A pharmacy dispenser fulfills prescriptions by coordinating a fixed set of
participants -- pharmacist verification, inventory debit, and insurance
billing -- through a two-phase commit. For each prescription, every
participant casts a yes or no vote; once every participant has voted yes and
none has voted no, the coordinator commits and the pharmacy performs the one
irreversible step, physically dispensing the medication to the patient. If
any participant votes no, the coordinator aborts and the prescription is
never dispensed through the normal path. A privileged pharmacist admin can
also force a commit on a prescription that already has a recorded no vote
(an emergency override, e.g. a manually approved substitution for an
out-of-stock item); once a prescription's outcome is settled -- committed or
aborted -- neither the normal commit path nor the admin override can act on
it again. Because dispensing medication cannot be undone, the two-phase
protocol and the admin override must never together let the same
prescription be dispensed more than once.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every prescription, the medication is dispensed at most
once, and it has been dispensed exactly when that prescription's status is
committed.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m8p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Agents, MaxWork

\* Every agent gets exactly one commit slot, so the version can never run
\* past the number of agents; that keeps the state space finite without
\* weakening the hierarchical-locking discipline being modeled.
MaxVersion == Cardinality(Agents)

\* coarseLock/fineLock model the two-level hierarchy: an agent must hold the
\* conveyor-segment lock before it may take the record's fine lock. myBase
\* is the version snapshot taken at fine-lock time; workLeft models an
\* agent that is slow-but-not-failed, needing several internal steps before
\* it is allowed to commit.
VARIABLES coarseLock, fineLock, recordVersion, myBase, workLeft, done

vars == <<coarseLock, fineLock, recordVersion, myBase, workLeft, done>>

Init ==
  /\ coarseLock = "none"
  /\ fineLock = "none"
  /\ recordVersion = 0
  /\ myBase = [a \in Agents |-> 0]
  /\ workLeft = [a \in Agents |-> 0]
  /\ done = [a \in Agents |-> FALSE]

AcquireCoarse(a) ==
  /\ ~done[a]
  /\ coarseLock = "none"
  /\ coarseLock' = a
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, recordVersion, myBase, workLeft, done>>

AcquireFine(a) ==
  /\ coarseLock = a
  /\ fineLock = "none"
  /\ fineLock' = a
  /\ myBase' = [myBase EXCEPT ![a] = recordVersion]
  /\ workLeft' = [workLeft EXCEPT ![a] = MaxWork]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, recordVersion, done>>

\* The slow-but-not-failed recomputation: any number of steps, but finite.
SlowStep(a) ==
  /\ fineLock = a
  /\ workLeft[a] > 0
  /\ workLeft' = [workLeft EXCEPT ![a] = @ - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLock, recordVersion, myBase, done>>

CommitUpdate(a) ==
  /\ fineLock = a
  /\ workLeft[a] = 0
  /\ recordVersion < MaxVersion
  /\ recordVersion' = recordVersion + 1
  /\ fineLock' = "none"
  /\ coarseLock' = "none"
  /\ done' = [done EXCEPT ![a] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<myBase, workLeft>>

Next ==
  \/ \E a \in Agents : AcquireCoarse(a)
  \/ \E a \in Agents : AcquireFine(a)
  \/ \E a \in Agents : SlowStep(a)
  \/ \E a \in Agents : CommitUpdate(a)

\* The two lock-acquisition steps compete across agents (enabledness can
\* flap as the locks pass around), so they need strong fairness; once an
\* agent actually holds the fine lock, nothing else can take it away, so
\* weak fairness is enough to make it keep working and then commit.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ (\A a \in Agents : SF_vars(AcquireCoarse(a)) /\ SF_vars(AcquireFine(a)))
  /\ (\A a \in Agents : WF_vars(SlowStep(a)) /\ WF_vars(CommitUpdate(a)))

\* Safety: while an agent holds the fine lock, its snapshot is still
\* current -- no lost update, because no other commit could have slipped
\* in underneath it during its (possibly long) recomputation.
NoLostUpdate ==
  \A a \in Agents : (fineLock = a) => (myBase[a] = recordVersion)

\* Liveness: every agent's update is eventually applied, no matter how
\* many SlowStep rounds it takes.
AllUpdatesApplied == \A a \in Agents : <> done[a]

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Agents = {a1, a2, a3}
  MaxWork = 2
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
PROPERTY AllUpdatesApplied
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An airport baggage router maintains one shared itinerary record per bag,
recording which gate the bag should be routed to next. A fixed set of
routing agents each need to apply exactly one update to this shared record
(a re-route triggered by a gate change, a missed connection, and so on).
To update the record, an agent first takes the coarse lock on the conveyor
segment carrying the bag, then takes the fine-grained lock on the itinerary
record itself; taking the fine lock also snapshots the record's current
version number for that agent. Only after that snapshot may the agent do the
(possibly slow) work of recomputing the new routing, one step at a time --
an agent can be arbitrarily slow doing this recomputation, but it is never
failed or abandoned, so it always eventually finishes. Once its work is
done, the agent commits: the record's version advances by one and both locks
are released together. Because the fine lock is held exclusively for the
whole snapshot-work-commit sequence, no agent's slow recomputation can ever
be silently overwritten by another agent's concurrent commit.

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever an agent currently holds the fine-grained lock on
the itinerary record, the version number it snapshotted when it acquired
that lock still equals the record's current version -- no concurrent commit
has slipped in underneath it.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every routing agent eventually finishes applying its
update to the shared record, however slowly it recomputes the new route.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od17m5p3t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Slots, Bags, Controllers, QuorumSize, NoBag

VARIABLES proposal, votes, assigned, adminLog

vars == <<proposal, votes, assigned, adminLog>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ proposal \in [Slots -> Bags \cup {NoBag}]
  /\ votes \in [Slots -> SUBSET Controllers]
  /\ assigned \subseteq (Slots \X Bags)
  /\ adminLog \subseteq Slots

NoDoubleAllocation ==
  \A s \in Slots : Cardinality({b \in Bags : <<s, b>> \in assigned}) <= 1

SlotFree(s) == ~ \E b \in Bags : <<s, b>> \in assigned

Init ==
  /\ proposal = [s \in Slots |-> NoBag]
  /\ votes = [s \in Slots |-> {}]
  /\ assigned = {}
  /\ adminLog = {}

Propose(s, b) ==
  /\ proposal[s] = NoBag
  /\ SlotFree(s)
  /\ proposal' = [proposal EXCEPT ![s] = b]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<assigned, adminLog>>

CastVote(s, c) ==
  /\ proposal[s] # NoBag
  /\ c \notin votes[s]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = @ \cup {c}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposal, assigned, adminLog>>

CommitAllocation(s) ==
  /\ proposal[s] # NoBag
  /\ Cardinality(votes[s]) >= QuorumSize
  /\ SlotFree(s)
  /\ assigned' = assigned \cup {<<s, proposal[s]>>}
  /\ proposal' = [proposal EXCEPT ![s] = NoBag]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED adminLog

ReleaseSlot(s, b) ==
  /\ <<s, b>> \in assigned
  /\ assigned' = assigned \ {<<s, b>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposal, votes, adminLog>>

AdminOverride(s, b) ==
  /\ SlotFree(s)
  /\ assigned' = assigned \cup {<<s, b>>}
  /\ adminLog' = adminLog \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposal, votes>>

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Slots, b \in Bags : Propose(s, b)
  \/ \E s \in Slots, c \in Controllers : CastVote(s, c)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : CommitAllocation(s)
  \/ \E s \in Slots, b \in Bags : ReleaseSlot(s, b)
  \/ \E s \in Slots, b \in Bags : AdminOverride(s, b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

THEOREM Spec => []NoDoubleAllocation
===============================================================================
nl:
An airport's automated baggage router assigns each checked bag to an available
induction slot chosen from a small pool of conveyor slots. Under normal
operation a proposal for a slot is not binding by itself: one of the router's
redundant control nodes proposes a candidate bag for a currently free slot,
and then a quorum of the router's control nodes must independently cast a
vote approving that specific proposal before the router commits the
assignment and the slot becomes occupied. Once a bag's assignment is
committed, the slot stays held for that bag until the bag physically clears
the induction point and the router releases the slot back to the free pool,
after which it can be proposed and voted on again for a different bag. To
handle exceptional situations (a security recall, a VIP bag jam, a hardware
fault on a scanner), a privileged airport-operations administrator may bypass
the normal propose/vote sequence entirely and force-assign a bag straight to
a slot -- but the router still refuses to let an admin's override land on a
slot that already holds a bag, so the override can add a new assignment but
can never silently clobber an existing one.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at every reachable state, each conveyor slot is bound to at
most one bag at a time, whether that binding was produced by the
propose-vote-commit quorum path or by the admin override path, and slots are
only ever freed by an explicit release.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od0m6p0t2 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Instances, MaxLease, MaxRenewals, NoInst

VARIABLES lease, ticksLeft, renewCount, requestPending, myLease

vars == <<lease, ticksLeft, renewCount, requestPending, myLease>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ lease \in Instances \cup {NoInst}
  /\ ticksLeft \in 0..MaxLease
  /\ renewCount \in 0..MaxRenewals
  /\ requestPending \in [Instances -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ myLease \in [Instances -> BOOLEAN]

MutualExclusion ==
  /\ \A i, j \in Instances : (i # j /\ myLease[i]) => ~myLease[j]
  /\ \A i \in Instances : myLease[i] => (lease = i)

EventualAcquire ==
  \A i \in Instances : [](requestPending[i] => <>(myLease[i]))

Init ==
  /\ lease = NoInst
  /\ ticksLeft = 0
  /\ renewCount = 0
  /\ requestPending = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]
  /\ myLease = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]

Request(i) ==
  /\ ~requestPending[i]
  /\ ~myLease[i]
  /\ requestPending' = [requestPending EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]

hospital's own scheduler and a satellite clinic's overflow scheduler -- that

operating room. Neither scheduler talks to the other directly; the only thing

scheduler is not starved. A scheduler may also voluntarily release the room
before its countdown reaches zero once the team is done. Because the two
schedulers are independent, each keeps its own local belief about whether it
currently holds the lease, separate from the shared lease record itself.

it holds the lease agrees with the shared lease record about who holds it.

runway configuration is currently in force at a busy airport. Controllers
submit proposed updates to that record (for example, switching the active

controller believed was current when it read the record. Whenever the
airport's configuration is formally reconfigured (a shift change, a weather
call, a new arrival flow), the allocator advances the record to a fresh
epoch, which fences out any proposal that was stamped with an older epoch.

arbitrarily, so a proposal stamped with a stale epoch can arrive well after
newer proposals or after an unrelated reconfiguration. The allocator commits
a proposal only if its stamped epoch still exactly matches the record's
current epoch; committing advances the epoch by one and appends the new

longer matches are discarded rather than applied, so a reordered, stale

logged value for the current epoch, so despite arbitrary message reordering
no committed update is ever lost or skipped.

nl:
Two independent settlement coordinators -- one at each of a bank's two data
centers -- draw from a single shared pool of leadership tickets to decide
who is allowed to execute today's interbank settlement batch, an action that
moves real money between correspondent accounts and can never be undone once
it happens. Leadership works by election with failover: whichever
coordinator instance wins an election is granted the current leadership
epoch as its own fencing token and is marked the pool's leader. A leader can
resign (or crash) at any time, which clears the pool's leader slot so a new
election can happen; a fresh election always advances the shared epoch
counter, so any token an old leader was still holding no longer matches the
pool's current epoch. A coordinator is only permitted to execute the
settlement batch while its own remembered fencing token still equals the
pool's current epoch, which is exactly what stops a coordinator that lost
leadership from double-settling after a failover has moved the pool on to a
fresh epoch. A coordinator that notices its remembered token is stale may
discard it. Because the settlement is irreversible, once it has executed once
it can never execute again.

failover, the interbank settlement batch executes at most once.

through failover, the interbank settlement batch is eventually executed.

nl:
A library's book reservation system manages a fixed number of physical
copies of a title. Every copy is at all times either sitting on the shelf as
available, checked out on hold for a patron as reserved, or momentarily held
in escrow while a reservation is being agreed upon. Placing a hold on a copy
requires a two-phase commit between the two participants that jointly own
the decision: the branch's shelf ledger and the library system's central
holds ledger. First a copy is pulled from the available shelf into escrow
and a transaction begins. Each participant then casts its vote to confirm
the hold. Only once both participants have voted does the transaction commit
and the escrowed copy becomes officially reserved; if the transaction has not
yet received both votes it may instead be aborted, which returns the
escrowed copy to the shelf as available again. A reservation can also end
normally when the hold expires or the patron returns the book, which moves
that copy from reserved back to available. Finally, a privileged library
administrator can force an in-flight transaction to be abandoned at any
time -- even after both participants have already voted to commit -- for
example to comply with an urgent recall notice; the forced abandonment
always returns the escrowed copy to the shelf rather than making it vanish.

plus the number of reserved copies, plus the number of copies currently in
an escrowed in-flight transaction, equals the fixed total number of copies
of the title -- no copy is ever created or destroyed by any of the six
actions (begin hold, vote, commit, ordinary abort, normal release of an
expired or returned reservation, or admin-forced abandonment).

bins ("slots") used to stage filled prescriptions until the patient arrives
for pickup. Each bin is guarded by a compare-and-swap register: a
prescription that wants a bin must first observe an empty bin and then
perform an atomic compare-and-swap that only succeeds if the bin is still
empty at the moment of the swap; if another prescription claimed it first,
the CAS fails and the loser retries against a different bin. The number of
active bins is not fixed - the pharmacy manager brings additional bins
online during rush hours and takes them offline during quiet periods, so the
range of usable bin numbers changes at runtime, while any prescription
already staged in a now-out-of-range bin is left undisturbed until the
patient picks it up. Once a patient collects a prescription, its bin is
cleared and becomes available for a future compare-and-swap. Because staging
depends on a compare-and-swap register instead of a single centrally
serialized clerk, the system must guarantee that no bin is ever awarded to
two prescriptions at once, and that each prescription's own memory of which
bin it holds always agrees with the register.

occupies always matches that bin's compare-and-swap register, and no two
prescriptions ever simultaneously believe they occupy the same bin.

eventually staged into a bin and picked up by the patient.

whose epoch tag no longer matches its current epoch, so a straggling,

printing simply releases the press for the next acquire.

resource at any time, and whenever a station holds it, that hold was
granted under the epoch that is still current.

nl:
A stock exchange runs its opening auction across a small cluster of
matching-engine replicas so that no single node's failure can stall the
open. Before any customer order is admitted into the auction's opening
book, the replicas must independently vote on admitting it, and only once
a quorum of replicas has voted yes is the order actually committed to the
book. Order-proposal and vote messages travel over an asynchronous replica
network that can reorder them arbitrarily -- a vote for one order can
arrive after votes for an order proposed later, and votes for the same
order can arrive at different replicas in different orders -- but because
quorum counting only cares about which replicas eventually voted, not the
order they arrived in, the exchange's admission decisions never depend on
message order. What the exchange must still guarantee is that the fixed
depth of the opening book is never exceeded: an order may pass an
optimistic depth check at proposal time and still lose the race to other
concurrently committing orders, so the matching engine re-checks the book's
remaining capacity at the moment of commit, and once the book is full the
auction closes to further admissions.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The auction's opening book never holds more committed
orders than its fixed capacity, and every committed order is backed by a
genuine quorum of replica votes.

nl:
A wildfire surveillance swarm of drones patrols a forest sector, and only
one drone at a time is authorized to transmit fire-detection alerts back to
the ground station, to avoid conflicting or duplicate alarms. Command
authority is granted through a compare-and-swap register: a drone may
claim command only while the register reads empty, and claiming it
atomically stamps the drone with a fresh, strictly higher fencing term.
Because the swarm operates over unreliable radio links in remote terrain,
at most one drone can crash silently while holding command -- it simply
stops responding, but the register keeps naming it as commander until a
ground-station watchdog notices the silence and revokes the stale
registration, freeing the register for a healthy drone to reclaim. No
drone may transmit a wildfire alert unless it currently holds the register
and has not (yet) been marked crashed, so neither an unauthorized drone nor
a stale, silently-crashed former commander can ever get its transmission
counted as an authoritative alert.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every wildfire alert transmitted is attributable to
exactly the drone that legitimately won that alert's fencing term via
compare-and-swap; no unauthorized or stale participant's transmission is
ever logged under a term it never held.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Despite at most one drone silently crashing while in
command, the swarm eventually transmits a wildfire alert under a legitimately
command term.

CONSTANTS Orders, Slots, NoOwner

VARIABLES slotOwner, msgs, allocLog, unallocated, triedSlots, gaveUp

vars == <<slotOwner, msgs, allocLog, unallocated, triedSlots, gaveUp>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ slotOwner \in [Slots -> Orders \cup {NoOwner}]
  /\ msgs \subseteq [order: Orders, slot: Slots]
  /\ allocLog \subseteq (Orders \X Slots)
  /\ unallocated \subseteq Orders
  /\ triedSlots \in [Orders -> SUBSET Slots]
  /\ gaveUp \subseteq Orders

Init ==
  /\ slotOwner = [s \in Slots |-> NoOwner]
  /\ msgs = {}
  /\ allocLog = {}
  /\ unallocated = Orders
  /\ triedSlots = [o \in Orders |-> {}]
  /\ gaveUp = {}

Submit(o, s) ==
  /\ o \in unallocated
  /\ o \notin gaveUp
  /\ s \notin triedSlots[o]
  /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {[order |-> o, slot |-> s]}
  /\ triedSlots' = [triedSlots EXCEPT ![o] = @ \cup {s}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, allocLog, unallocated, gaveUp>>

Deliver(m) ==
  /\ m \in msgs
  /\ msgs' = msgs \ {m}
  /\ IF slotOwner[m.slot] = NoOwner /\ m.order \in unallocated
       THEN /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![m.slot] = m.order]
            /\ allocLog' = allocLog \cup {<<m.order, m.slot>>}
            /\ unallocated' = unallocated \ {m.order}
       ELSE UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, allocLog, unallocated>>
  /\ UNCHANGED <<triedSlots, gaveUp>>

DropStale(m) ==
  /\ m \in msgs
  /\ m.order \notin unallocated
  /\ msgs' = msgs \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, allocLog, unallocated, triedSlots, gaveUp>>

Abandon(o) ==
  /\ o \in unallocated
  /\ o \notin gaveUp
  /\ triedSlots[o] = Slots
  /\ gaveUp' = gaveUp \cup {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, msgs, allocLog, unallocated, triedSlots>>

Terminated == /\ msgs = {}
              /\ \A o \in Orders : o \notin unallocated \/ o \in gaveUp
Idle == Terminated /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
  \/ \E o \in Orders, s \in Slots : Submit(o, s)
  \/ \E m \in msgs : Deliver(m)
  \/ \E m \in msgs : DropStale(m)
  \/ \E o \in Orders : Abandon(o)
  \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAllocation ==
  \A p1, p2 \in allocLog : p1[2] = p2[2] => p1[1] = p2[1]

===============================================================================
nl:
A stock exchange runs a pre-open auction that must assign each arriving order
to one of a small number of priority allocation slots before the opening
cross. Each slot is backed by a compare-and-swap (CAS) register: a slot's
register starts empty, and a claim only succeeds if the register is still
empty at the moment the claim is applied. Orders submit slot-claim messages
into the exchange's inbound network, but that network is not FIFO -- claim
messages can be reordered in transit, so they may be delivered in a different
order than they were sent, and an order may have several claim messages for
different candidate slots in flight at once. When a claim message is
delivered, the CAS either succeeds (the slot's register was still empty and
the order was still unresolved, so the order now owns that slot) or fails
silently (the slot was already taken, or the order already got resolved by
another claim first). A claim message that arrives for an order that has
already been resolved by an earlier delivery is recognized as stale and
discarded without effect. An order that has tried every slot and still holds
none gives up and abandons the auction. The exchange keeps an append-only
confirmation log of every winning CAS so its allocation history can be
audited. Once every order has either won a slot or abandoned, and no claim
messages remain in flight, the auction sits quiescent with nothing left to
process. SAFETY PROPERTY: the confirmation log never records two different
orders as having won the same allocation slot.

  /\ inCS \subseteq Coordinators
  /\ campaigning \subseteq Coordinators
  /\ votesFor \in [Coordinators -> SUBSET Voters]
  /\ pendingVotes \in [Coordinators -> SUBSET Voters]

Init ==
  /\ holder = NoHolder
  /\ inCS = {}
  /\ campaigning = {}
  /\ votesFor = [c \in Coordinators |-> {}]
  /\ pendingVotes = [c \in Coordinators |-> {}]

Campaign(c) ==
  /\ c \notin campaigning
  /\ c \notin inCS
  /\ campaigning' = campaigning \cup {c}
  /\ votesFor' = [votesFor EXCEPT ![c] = {}]
  /\ pendingVotes' = [pendingVotes EXCEPT ![c] = Voters]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, inCS>>

VoteRespond(c, v) ==
  /\ c \in campaigning
  /\ v \in pendingVotes[c]
  /\ pendingVotes' = [pendingVotes EXCEPT ![c] = @ \ {v}]
  /\ votesFor' = [votesFor EXCEPT ![c] = @ \cup {v}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, inCS, campaigning>>

  /\ holder = NoHolder
  /\ 2 * Cardinality(votesFor[c]) > Cardinality(Voters)
  /\ holder' = c

  /\ pendingVotes' = [pendingVotes EXCEPT ![c] = {}]

  /\ holder = c
  /\ holder' = NoHolder
  /\ inCS' = inCS \ {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<campaigning, votesFor, pendingVotes>>

  \/ \E c \in Coordinators : Campaign(c)
  \/ \E c \in Coordinators, v \in Voters : VoteRespond(c, v)
  \/ \E c \in Coordinators : Acquire(c)
  \/ \E c \in Coordinators : Release(c)

             /\ \A c \in Coordinators : \A v \in Voters : WF_vars(VoteRespond(c, v))

MutualExclusion == \A c \in inCS : holder = c

VotesEventuallyAnswered ==
  \A c \in Coordinators : (pendingVotes[c] # {}) ~> (pendingVotes[c] = {})

PROPERTY VotesEventuallyAnswered
nl:
A small group of settlement coordinators takes turns running a bank's
interbank settlement batch, a critical operation that must never be executed
by more than one coordinator at once. Before a coordinator may run the
batch it must campaign for the exclusive settlement lock: it sends a vote
request to every member of a fixed panel of voting banks, and only when it
has collected votes from a majority of that panel may it acquire the lock
and enter the critical section. Voting banks can be slow to respond -- a
vote can sit unanswered for an arbitrarily long time -- but a voting bank
never fails outright, so every vote request it receives is eventually
answered. A coordinator that acquires the lock later releases it once the
batch is done, and any leftover unanswered votes for that campaign are
cancelled at that point. Four things can happen: a coordinator starts a new
campaign, a voting bank answers one of its outstanding vote requests, a
campaigning coordinator with a majority of votes acquires the lock (only if
it is currently free), and a coordinator holding the lock releases it.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a coordinator considers itself inside the
settlement critical section, it is in fact the coordinator currently
recorded as holding the exclusive lock.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every outstanding vote request eventually gets answered,
so a campaigning coordinator's set of unanswered votes always eventually
empties out.

CONSTANTS Students, Replicas, Capacity

VARIABLES enrolled, pending, votes, responded, msgs, rejected

vars == <<enrolled, pending, votes, responded, msgs, rejected>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ enrolled \subseteq Students
  /\ pending \subseteq Students
  /\ votes \in [Students -> SUBSET Replicas]
  /\ responded \in [Students -> SUBSET Replicas]
  /\ msgs \subseteq [student: Students, replica: Replicas]
  /\ rejected \subseteq Students

Init ==
  /\ enrolled = {}
  /\ pending = {}
  /\ votes = [s \in Students |-> {}]
  /\ responded = [s \in Students |-> {}]
  /\ msgs = {}
  /\ rejected = {}

Request(s) ==
  /\ s \notin pending
  /\ s \notin enrolled
  /\ s \notin rejected
  /\ pending' = pending \cup {s}
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
  /\ responded' = [responded EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
  /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {[student |-> s, replica |-> r] : r \in Replicas}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, rejected>>

DeliverVote(m) ==
  /\ m \in msgs
  /\ msgs' = msgs \ {m}
  /\ responded' = [responded EXCEPT ![m.student] = @ \cup {m.replica}]
  /\ IF Cardinality(enrolled) < Capacity
       THEN votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![m.student] = @ \cup {m.replica}]
       ELSE UNCHANGED votes
  /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, pending, rejected>>

HasMajority(s) == 2 * Cardinality(votes[s]) > Cardinality(Replicas)

Commit(s) ==
  /\ s \in pending
  /\ HasMajority(s)
  /\ Cardinality(enrolled) < Capacity
  /\ enrolled' = enrolled \cup {s}
  /\ pending' = pending \ {s}
  /\ msgs' = {m \in msgs : m.student # s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, responded, rejected>>

Reject(s) ==
  /\ s \in pending
  /\ responded[s] = Replicas
  /\ ~(HasMajority(s) /\ Cardinality(enrolled) < Capacity)
  /\ pending' = pending \ {s}
  /\ rejected' = rejected \cup {s}
  /\ msgs' = {m \in msgs : m.student # s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, votes, responded>>

Terminated == /\ msgs = {}
              /\ \A s \in Students : s \in enrolled \/ s \in rejected
Idle == Terminated /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Students : Request(s)
  \/ \E m \in msgs : DeliverVote(m)
  \/ \E s \in Students : Commit(s)
  \/ \E s \in Students : Reject(s)
  \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityRespected == Cardinality(enrolled) <= Capacity

nl:
A university course-registration system enforces a hard seat cap on a
popular course by having a small panel of registrar replicas vote on every
enrollment attempt before it is finalized. When a student requests a seat,
the registrar broadcasts a vote-request to every replica in the panel. The
inbound network is not FIFO, so those vote-request messages -- for the same
student or for different students racing for the last seats -- can be
delivered to replicas in any order, out of the order they were sent. A
replica votes to approve a request only if, at the moment it looks, the
course does not yet appear full. A student's enrollment is finalized only
once a majority of the panel has approved it, and even then the system
re-checks the live seat count at the moment of finalization (because by
then, concurrent commits racing ahead of a reordered vote may have already
filled the remaining seats): if the seat count is still below capacity the
student is enrolled and any of that student's still-outstanding vote
messages are cancelled, otherwise the request is rejected outright and the
student does not retry. Four things can happen: a student requests a seat, a
replica delivers and casts one outstanding vote, a majority-approved request
with a seat still available is committed, and a request for which every
replica has now responded but that never reached a live majority is
rejected. Once every student has been enrolled or rejected and no vote
messages remain in flight, the registration round sits quiescent with
nothing left to process. SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of students ever
enrolled in the course never exceeds its seat capacity.

nl:
A wildfire surveillance swarm of drones is coordinated by a ground control
station that periodically reconfigures the fleet's mission parameters by
advancing a global epoch number and issuing a fresh directive, tagged with
that epoch, to every drone. Each drone tracks the highest epoch it has
personally adopted, and it only ever carries out a directive whose tag
exactly matches its own currently adopted epoch -- this is how the swarm
fences off stale or unauthorized instructions left over from a previous
configuration. A drone can be slow to catch up to a new epoch (smoke,
weak signal, or a long flight leg can delay it for a long time), but it
never fails outright, so it always eventually catches up. A directive that
is still sitting undelivered after the drone has already moved past its
epoch is recognized as stale and thrown away rather than executed. Four
things can happen: ground control advances the epoch and re-issues
directives to every drone, a drone catches up its adopted epoch to the
current one, a drone carries out a directive whose tag matches its adopted
epoch, and a drone discards a leftover directive whose tag is now older
than its adopted epoch. Once the epoch counter has reached its configured
ceiling, every drone has caught up, and no directive is left outstanding,
the swarm settles with nothing left to do. SAFETY PROPERTY: every directive
a drone actually carries out is recorded together with the drone's adopted
epoch at that exact moment, and the two always agree -- a drone never
carries out a directive under an epoch that was not its own currently
authorized one.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: whenever a drone has fallen behind the current epoch, it
eventually catches up to it.

  /\ localVersion \in [Robots -> 0..MaxVersion]

  /\ localVersion = [r \in Robots |-> 0]

  /\ localVersion[r] # version

  \/ \E r \in Robots : RetryStaleRead(r)
  \/ \E r \in Robots : Commit(r)
  \/ \E r \in Robots : AdminOverride(r)
  \/ \E r \in Robots : Depart(r)

CONSTANTS
  Robots = {r1, r2, r3, r4}
  Capacity = 2
  MaxVersion = 3

nl:
A warehouse robot fleet shares a single staging bay with a hard capacity
limit. A robot that wants to park in the bay uses optimistic concurrency
control: it first reads the bay's current version number, then, once it has
decided to park, tries to commit by checking that the version has not
changed since it read it and that the bay still has room. If the version
has moved on -- another robot committed in between -- the commit is
rejected and the robot simply re-reads the current version and retries
later rather than blocking. Separately, a privileged fleet-operations admin
can force a robot straight into the bay without going through the
read/retry protocol at all, skipping the version check entirely; but the
admin override still has to obey the bay's physical capacity -- it may only
force a robot in if the bay currently has room, because the capacity limit
is a hard physical constraint, not a concurrency-control artifact. A robot
in the bay eventually departs, which frees a slot and bumps the version
counter. Five things can happen: an idle robot reads the current version
and begins trying to park, an attempting robot whose read version is now
stale re-reads the fresh version, an attempting robot whose version still
matches commits into the bay (only if there is room), the admin forces any
non-parked robot straight into the bay (only if there is room), and a
parked robot departs the bay. SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of robots parked
in the staging bay never exceeds its capacity.

VARIABLES coarseLock, fineLock, record, pc, target

vars == <<coarseLock, fineLock, record, pc, target>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ coarseLock \in Cranes \cup {NoOne}
  /\ fineLock \in [Records -> Cranes \cup {NoOne}]
  /\ record \in [Records -> 0..MaxRecord]
  /\ pc \in [Cranes -> {"idle", "reqFine", "update", "release"}]
  /\ target \in [Cranes -> Records]

Init ==
  /\ coarseLock = NoOne
  /\ fineLock = [r \in Records |-> NoOne]
  /\ record = [r \in Records |-> 0]
  /\ pc = [c \in Cranes |-> "idle"]
  /\ target \in [Cranes -> Records]

RequestCoarse(c) ==
  /\ pc[c] = "idle"
  /\ coarseLock = NoOne
  /\ \E r \in Records: target' = [target EXCEPT ![c] = r]
  /\ coarseLock' = c
  /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![c] = "reqFine"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, record>>

RequestFine(c) ==
  /\ pc[c] = "reqFine"
  /\ coarseLock = c
  /\ fineLock[target[c]] = NoOne
  /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![target[c]] = c]
  /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![c] = "update"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, record, target>>

PerformUpdate(c) ==
  /\ pc[c] = "update"
  /\ fineLock[target[c]] = c
  /\ record' = [record EXCEPT ![target[c]] = (@ + 1) % (MaxRecord + 1)]
  /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![c] = "release"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLock, target>>

ReleaseLocks(c) ==
  /\ pc[c] = "release"
  /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![target[c]] = NoOne]
  /\ coarseLock' = NoOne
  /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, target>>

Next ==
  \E c \in Cranes:
    \/ RequestCoarse(c)
    \/ RequestFine(c)
    \/ PerformUpdate(c)
    \/ ReleaseLocks(c)

  /\ (\A c \in Cranes:
        /\ WF_vars(RequestCoarse(c))
        /\ WF_vars(RequestFine(c))
        /\ WF_vars(PerformUpdate(c))
        /\ WF_vars(ReleaseLocks(c)))

NoLostUpdates ==

EventuallyIdle == \A c \in Cranes: (pc[c] # "idle") ~> (pc[c] = "idle")

  Records = {r1, r2}
  NoOne = NoOne
  MaxRecord = 3
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
PROPERTY EventuallyIdle
nl:
A container-ship crane yard maintains a shared ledger of per-bay container tallies. Before a crane may touch the ledger it must acquire a yard-wide coarse lock, and then, while still holding the coarse lock, a bay-specific fine lock for the record it intends to update. Only after holding both locks may the crane perform its update; it then releases both locks together and returns to idle. Any number of cranes can be cycling through this protocol concurrently, and a crane may take an arbitrarily long time working through its own phases -- it is never removed from contention or considered failed, just occasionally slow to act. The system has four actions: a crane requests the coarse lock and simultaneously picks the bay record it means to touch, it requests the fine lock on that record once it holds the coarse lock, it performs the update to the record once it holds both locks, and it releases both locks and returns to idle.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any crane that is in the middle of updating (or about to release from) a record still actually holds both the coarse lock and that record's fine lock, so no concurrent crane can ever clobber an in-progress update -- no update is ever lost.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every crane that begins a request cycle eventually returns to idle, i.e. every crane that starts a request eventually gets to update its chosen record and release the locks, no matter how slow other cranes are about relinquishing the yard.

---- MODULE W4Od0m6p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Teams, Capacity, MaxGen

VARIABLES teamStatus, roomsInUse, gen, inFlight

vars == <<teamStatus, roomsInUse, gen, inFlight>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ teamStatus \in [Teams -> {"idle", "requesting", "holding"}]
  /\ roomsInUse \in 0..Capacity
  /\ gen \in [Teams -> 0..MaxGen]
  /\ inFlight \subseteq [team: Teams, g: 0..MaxGen]

Init ==
  /\ teamStatus = [t \in Teams |-> "idle"]
  /\ roomsInUse = 0
  /\ gen = [t \in Teams |-> 0]
  /\ inFlight = {}

Request(t) ==
  /\ teamStatus[t] = "idle"
  /\ gen[t] < MaxGen
  /\ gen' = [gen EXCEPT ![t] = @ + 1]
  /\ teamStatus' = [teamStatus EXCEPT ![t] = "requesting"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<roomsInUse, inFlight>>

CancelRequest(t) ==
  /\ teamStatus[t] = "requesting"
  /\ gen[t] < MaxGen
  /\ gen' = [gen EXCEPT ![t] = @ + 1]
  /\ teamStatus' = [teamStatus EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<roomsInUse, inFlight>>

Grant(t) ==
  /\ teamStatus[t] = "requesting"
  /\ roomsInUse < Capacity
  /\ ~ (\E m \in inFlight: m.team = t /\ m.g = gen[t])
  /\ roomsInUse' = roomsInUse + 1
  /\ inFlight' = inFlight \cup {[team |-> t, g |-> gen[t]]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<teamStatus, gen>>

DeliverGrant(m) ==
  /\ m \in inFlight
  /\ m.g = gen[m.team]
  /\ teamStatus[m.team] = "requesting"
  /\ teamStatus' = [teamStatus EXCEPT ![m.team] = "holding"]
  /\ inFlight' = inFlight \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<roomsInUse, gen>>

DropStale(m) ==
  /\ m \in inFlight
  /\ m.g # gen[m.team]
  /\ inFlight' = inFlight \ {m}
  /\ roomsInUse' = roomsInUse - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<teamStatus, gen>>

Expire(t) ==
  /\ teamStatus[t] = "holding"
  /\ teamStatus' = [teamStatus EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
  /\ roomsInUse' = roomsInUse - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, inFlight>>

Next ==
  \E t \in Teams:
    \/ Request(t)
    \/ CancelRequest(t)
    \/ Grant(t)
    \/ Expire(t)
    \/ (\E m \in inFlight: DeliverGrant(m) \/ DropStale(m))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityOK ==
  /\ Cardinality({t \in Teams : teamStatus[t] = "holding"}) <= Capacity
  /\ Cardinality({t \in Teams : teamStatus[t] = "holding"}) <= roomsInUse

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Teams = {t1, t2, t3}
  Capacity = 2
  MaxGen = 3
INVARIANT CapacityOK
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler leases out a fixed pool of operating rooms to surgical teams. When a team's request is granted, the scheduler immediately reserves a slot from the pool and sends the team a grant notice over the hospital network; the team only starts treating the room as its own once that notice actually arrives. Because the network can reorder messages, a grant notice can be delayed and delivered after the team has already given up and re-requested, or after its earlier lease was reclaimed. To guard against a stale, reordered notice being mistaken for a fresh one, every request carries a fencing token that the scheduler bumps whenever a team's request is abandoned or renewed; a delivered notice is only honored if its token still matches the team's current token, and a notice whose token no longer matches is simply discarded (and its reserved slot returned to the pool). A team can also spontaneously have its lease reclaimed (expire) once it is holding a room. The system has five actions: a team requests a room, a team cancels a pending request (bumping its fencing token), the scheduler grants a pending request by reserving a slot and emitting a notice, a team accepts a notice whose token still matches and starts holding the room, and either a stale notice is discarded and its slot released or a held lease expires and its slot is released.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of teams that believe they are currently holding an operating room never exceeds the room pool's capacity, and never exceeds the scheduler's own count of reserved slots, so a reordered or stale grant notice can never cause two teams to be double-booked into the same physical capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od19m3p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Nodes, Books, NoOne, MaxTerm

VARIABLES leader, term, pendingSet, finalizedSet, finalizeCount

vars == <<leader, term, pendingSet, finalizedSet, finalizeCount>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ leader \in Nodes \cup {NoOne}
  /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
  /\ pendingSet \subseteq Books
  /\ finalizedSet \subseteq Books
  /\ finalizeCount \in [Books -> 0..2]

Init ==
  /\ leader = NoOne
  /\ term = 0
  /\ pendingSet = {}
  /\ finalizedSet = {}
  /\ finalizeCount = [b \in Books |-> 0]

ElectLeader ==
  /\ leader = NoOne
  /\ \E n \in Nodes:
       leader' = n
  /\ term' = (term + 1) % (MaxTerm + 1)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pendingSet, finalizedSet, finalizeCount>>

StepDown ==
  /\ leader # NoOne
  /\ leader' = NoOne
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, pendingSet, finalizedSet, finalizeCount>>

RequestReservation(b) ==
  /\ b \notin pendingSet
  /\ b \notin finalizedSet
  /\ pendingSet' = pendingSet \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, finalizedSet, finalizeCount>>

Finalize(b) ==
  /\ leader # NoOne
  /\ b \in pendingSet
  /\ b \notin finalizedSet
  /\ finalizedSet' = finalizedSet \cup {b}
  /\ pendingSet' = pendingSet \ {b}
  /\ finalizeCount' = [finalizeCount EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term>>

AdminOverride(b) ==
  /\ b \notin finalizedSet
  /\ finalizedSet' = finalizedSet \cup {b}
  /\ pendingSet' = pendingSet \ {b}
  /\ finalizeCount' = [finalizeCount EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term>>

Next ==
  \/ ElectLeader
  \/ StepDown
  \/ (\E b \in Books: RequestReservation(b) \/ Finalize(b) \/ AdminOverride(b))

Spec ==
  Init /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(ElectLeader)
  /\ (\A b \in Books: SF_vars(Finalize(b)))

AtMostOnce ==
  \A b \in Books:
    /\ finalizeCount[b] <= 1
    /\ (b \in finalizedSet) => (finalizeCount[b] = 1)

EventualFinalize == \A b \in Books: (b \in pendingSet) ~> (b \in finalizedSet)

CONSTANTS
  Nodes = {n1, n2}
  Books = {b1, b2}
  NoOne = NoOne
  MaxTerm = 3
INVARIANT AtMostOnce
PROPERTY EventualFinalize
nl:
A library federation runs a reservation system across several branch servers. At any moment at most one branch server is the elected leader, and only the leader may finalize a reservation -- an irreversible action representing the book being physically pulled from the shelf and shipped to the requesting patron, which can never be undone or redone. Leadership is not stable: the current leader can step down (fail over) at any time, and a fresh election then picks a replacement, possibly leaving the system briefly leaderless. Separately, a privileged library administrator can force-finalize any not-yet-finalized reservation directly, bypassing the normal request queue and without needing a leader to be in place at all -- but the same already finalized guard applies to the admin's action as to the leader's, so even the override can never re-trigger the irreversible shipment for a book that has already gone out. The system has five actions: a fresh leader is elected whenever the branch is leaderless, the current leader steps down (triggering the need for a new election), a patron's reservation request becomes pending, the leader finalizes a pending, not-yet-finalized reservation, and the admin force-finalizes any not-yet-finalized reservation regardless of its pending status or of whether a leader currently exists.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every book, the irreversible finalize/shipment step -- whether performed by the elected leader or by the admin override -- fires at most once, and a book is recorded as finalized exactly when its finalize step has fired exactly that one time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every reservation that becomes pending is eventually finalized, no matter how many times leadership churns through elections and step-downs in the meantime.

EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cranes, MaxCap

VARIABLES occupied, capacity, craneState, readSnapshot

vars == <<occupied, capacity, craneState, readSnapshot>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ occupied \in 0..MaxCap
  /\ capacity \in 0..MaxCap
  /\ craneState \in [Cranes -> {"idle", "reading", "committing"}]
  /\ readSnapshot \in [Cranes -> 0..MaxCap]

Init ==
  /\ occupied = 0
  /\ capacity = MaxCap
  /\ craneState = [c \in Cranes |-> "idle"]
  /\ readSnapshot = [c \in Cranes |-> 0]

BeginPlace(c) ==
  /\ craneState[c] = "idle"
  /\ readSnapshot' = [readSnapshot EXCEPT ![c] = occupied]
  /\ craneState' = [craneState EXCEPT ![c] = "reading"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occupied, capacity>>

CommitPlace(c) ==
  /\ craneState[c] = "reading"
  /\ readSnapshot[c] = occupied
  /\ occupied < capacity
  /\ occupied' = occupied + 1
  /\ craneState' = [craneState EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, readSnapshot>>

RetryPlace(c) ==
  /\ craneState[c] = "reading"
  /\ readSnapshot[c] # occupied
  /\ readSnapshot' = [readSnapshot EXCEPT ![c] = occupied]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occupied, capacity, craneState>>

RemoveContainer ==
  /\ occupied > 0
  /\ occupied' = occupied - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, craneState, readSnapshot>>

ChangeCapacity ==
  /\ \E newCap \in occupied..MaxCap: capacity' = newCap
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occupied, craneState, readSnapshot>>

Next ==
  \/ (\E c \in Cranes: BeginPlace(c) \/ CommitPlace(c) \/ RetryPlace(c))
  \/ RemoveContainer
  \/ ChangeCapacity

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityHeld == occupied <= capacity

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Cranes = {c1, c2, c3}
  MaxCap = 3
INVARIANT CapacityHeld
nl:
A container-ship crane yard has a storage capacity that yard management can raise or lower at runtime, for example to open a new bay or close one for weather. Cranes placing containers into the yard do not take locks; instead each crane uses optimistic concurrency: it first reads the current number of stored containers as a snapshot, then attempts to commit its placement. A commit only succeeds if the occupied count has not changed since the snapshot was taken and the yard still has room under whatever the capacity limit currently is; otherwise the crane's optimistic check fails and it must retry by taking a fresh snapshot and trying again. Separately, containers can be removed from the yard at any time, and yard management can change the capacity bound at any time, though it may never set the new bound below the number of containers physically already sitting in the yard (existing containers are never evicted just because the limit was lowered). The system has five actions: a crane begins a placement attempt by snapshotting the occupied count, a crane commits its placement when its snapshot is still valid and there is room under the live capacity, a crane whose snapshot has gone stale retries by taking a fresh snapshot, a container is removed from the yard, and yard management changes the capacity bound to any value at least as large as the current occupied count.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of containers currently stored in the yard never exceeds the yard's current capacity bound, even though that bound can move at runtime while cranes have optimistic placements in flight.

---- MODULE W4Od0m8p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Teams, ORs, NoOne, PrepSteps

VARIABLES wardLock, orLock, pc, target, prepCount

vars == <<wardLock, orLock, pc, target, prepCount>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ wardLock \in Teams \cup {NoOne}
  /\ orLock \in [ORs -> Teams \cup {NoOne}]
  /\ pc \in [Teams -> {"idle", "wantOR", "prepping", "operating", "releasing"}]
  /\ target \in [Teams -> ORs]
  /\ prepCount \in [Teams -> 0..PrepSteps]

Init ==
  /\ wardLock = NoOne
  /\ orLock = [r \in ORs |-> NoOne]
  /\ pc = [t \in Teams |-> "idle"]
  /\ target \in [Teams -> ORs]
  /\ prepCount = [t \in Teams |-> 0]

AcquireWard(t) ==
  /\ pc[t] = "idle"
  /\ wardLock = NoOne
  /\ \E r \in ORs: target' = [target EXCEPT ![t] = r]
  /\ wardLock' = t
  /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![t] = "wantOR"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<orLock, prepCount>>

AcquireOR(t) ==
  /\ pc[t] = "wantOR"
  /\ wardLock = t
  /\ orLock[target[t]] = NoOne
  /\ orLock' = [orLock EXCEPT ![target[t]] = t]
  /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![t] = "prepping"]
  /\ prepCount' = [prepCount EXCEPT ![t] = PrepSteps]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<wardLock, target>>

Prep(t) ==
  /\ pc[t] = "prepping"
  /\ prepCount[t] > 0
  /\ prepCount' = [prepCount EXCEPT ![t] = @ - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<wardLock, orLock, pc, target>>

BeginSurgery(t) ==
  /\ pc[t] = "prepping"
  /\ prepCount[t] = 0
  /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![t] = "operating"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<wardLock, orLock, target, prepCount>>

FinishSurgery(t) ==
  /\ pc[t] = "operating"
  /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![t] = "releasing"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<wardLock, orLock, target, prepCount>>

ReleaseAll(t) ==
  /\ pc[t] = "releasing"
  /\ orLock' = [orLock EXCEPT ![target[t]] = NoOne]
  /\ wardLock' = NoOne
  /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<target, prepCount>>

Next ==
  \E t \in Teams:
    \/ AcquireWard(t)
    \/ AcquireOR(t)
    \/ Prep(t)
    \/ BeginSurgery(t)
    \/ FinishSurgery(t)
    \/ ReleaseAll(t)

Spec ==
  Init /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ (\A t \in Teams:
        /\ WF_vars(AcquireWard(t))
        /\ WF_vars(AcquireOR(t))
        /\ WF_vars(Prep(t))
        /\ WF_vars(BeginSurgery(t))
        /\ WF_vars(FinishSurgery(t))
        /\ WF_vars(ReleaseAll(t)))

MutualExclusion ==
  /\ \A r \in ORs: Cardinality({t \in Teams : pc[t] = "operating" /\ target[t] = r}) <= 1
  /\ \A t \in Teams: pc[t] = "operating" => orLock[target[t]] = t

EventuallyOperates == \A t \in Teams: (pc[t] = "wantOR") ~> (pc[t] = "operating")

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Teams = {t1, t2, t3}
  ORs = {r1, r2}
  NoOne = NoOne
  PrepSteps = 2
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
PROPERTY EventuallyOperates
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler uses hierarchical locking to protect access to its operating rooms. A surgical team first takes a ward-wide coarse lock and, while holding it, picks the specific operating room it wants; it then takes that room's own fine-grained lock. Only after holding both locks does the team begin its preparation checklist, which can take several ticks to complete -- the team is simply slow to get through the checklist, never stuck or failed, and it always eventually finishes it. Once preparation is done the team enters the operating room and performs surgery, then finishes and releases both locks together, returning the ward to availability for the next team. The system has six actions: a team acquires the coarse ward lock and picks its target room, a team acquires that room's fine lock once it holds the ward lock, a team ticks down one step of its (possibly slow) preparation checklist, a team begins surgery once its checklist has reached zero, a team finishes surgery, and a team releases both the room's fine lock and the ward lock together and returns to idle.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one team is ever actually operating in a given operating room at the same time, and any team recorded as operating in a room genuinely still holds that room's fine lock.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every team that has acquired the ward lock and is waiting on its room eventually gets to operate, regardless of how many preparation ticks it or anyone else needs.
